method: Tools/texloop/waterline/measure_waterline.py: the line is traced along the hull and compared with the clean gelcoat 0.6-1.6 cm above it, so the numbers are relative (CIE Y ratio and Lab difference) and hold under any light. Heights use a known-size object in frame. Round 3: the line's colour is the mean over its full width at half depth, and the targets are judged on the hero render (score_render.py), lit and tone-mapped like the photo; the swatches (flat albedo) are a quick proxy and read darker.

photos.what: TX 7295 EC (J/22, North Texas Sailing School) on a drive-on lift at Rush Creek Yacht Club, Lake Ray Hubbard, Oct 4 2026, overcast
photos.licence: Bean's own photo; measure only, never committed (shows people elsewhere in the frame)
photos.scale: Texas registration letters, 3 in (7.6 cm) = 105 px -> 13.8 px/cm at the bow quarter

measured.notes: A thin, ragged, nearly neutral grey line (not brown), with faint grey drip streaks above it. The bottom below reads darker partly because the hull turns away from the sky there, so below_Y_ratio is an upper bound on the film.
measured.method_note: line colour = mean over the line's full width at half depth (round 3; round 1 used the 3 darkest rows: 0.811)

photos.what: Same photo, the slip-kept cruisers behind (DALLAS TX transom and its neighbour): only a faint dark line at the water, no brown band or slime visible at about 15 m
photos.measured: too far for numbers; supports 'kept boats on this lake are clean'

sources_text.what: Fresh-water waterline stains are tea-coloured from tannins and silt; oxalic-acid cleaners remove them; lifts and waxing prevent them
Growth starts as a green slime film of single-celled algae, strongest at the waterline where the light is
Lake Ray Hubbard is fresh water and only 'suspect' for zebra mussels: no shells or crust
sources_text.url: texture loop plan, Lake not sea
